---
title: "Quiz · Define a capsule"
---

A short knowledge check. Answers are hidden behind callouts so you
can self-grade after answering.

## 1. Which fields are required on an `apiVersion: open-engineering.io/v1alpha1`, `kind: Capsule` at v0.1?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
`apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name`, `metadata.version`,
`spec.capability`, `spec.inputs`, `spec.outputs`,
`spec.dependencies`. See
[memo1 §1](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo1.md#1-required-field-set-minimal)
at `bf071c2c1b57`.
:::

## 2. Which of these identifiers are valid capability identifiers under the memo2 §3 D3 grammar? Explain each rejection.

a. `oe.greeting`
b. `github.issue.create`
c. `Greeting`
d. `oe..greeting`
e. `oe_greeting`
f. `pico.state.set`

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Valid: **a, b, f** — each is two or more lower-case dotted segments
whose first character is a lower-case letter and whose remaining
characters are lower-case letters, digits, or single internal
hyphens.

Invalid:

- **c (`Greeting`)** — single segment and starts with an upper-case
  letter.
- **d (`oe..greeting`)** — empty segment between the two dots.
- **e (`oe_greeting`)** — underscore is not in the segment alphabet
  and there is no dot separator.

See [memo2 §3 D3](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo2.md#3-d3--capability-identifier-grammar-and-2-amendment).
:::

## 3. A Pico ships at `oe.greeting@0.1.0`. The capsule maintainer wants to add an optional `locale` input. What is the smallest conformant next version, and why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
`0.2.0` — a **minor** bump. The memo2 §2 D2 breaking-change table
classifies **"Add an optional `spec.inputs` entry (with no
`required: true`)"** as compatible / minor: no existing consumer
breaks because every previously-required input is still required,
no existing type changed, and the new input is omitted-by-default.
See [memo2 §2 D2](https://github.com/open-engineering-capsules/source/blob/bf071c2c1b57/memo2.md#2-d2--version-compatibility-rule).
:::

## 4. The same maintainer then wants to remove the `greeting` output entirely. What is the next version, and why?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
`1.0.0` — a **major** bump. The memo2 §2 D2 breaking-change table
lists **"Remove a declared `spec.outputs` entry"** as breaking /
major: callers that read `greeting` from the previous contract no
longer see it. A `0.3.0` would silently violate the contract.
:::

## 5. memo1 §1 lists `spec.config`, `spec.secrets`, `spec.lifecycle`, `spec.compatibility`, `spec.health`, `spec.tests`, `spec.permissions`, and `spec.resources` as optional at v0.1. Pick two and give the one-line rationale memo1 §1 records for each.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
Any two of (memo1 §1):

- `spec.config` / `spec.secrets` — memo23 §5 rule 8 (Secure
  configuration) applies when a capsule needs them; many capsules
  (e.g. the Module 3 greeting) need neither.
- `spec.lifecycle` — memo23 §5 rule 1 (Minimal core) keeps
  lifecycle on the Pico runtime, not inside every capsule.
- `spec.compatibility` — memo23 §5 rule 6 is already met by
  `metadata.version` plus the memo2 §2 D2 constraint forms at
  v0.1; richer constraints are a later concern.
- `spec.health` / `spec.tests` — memo23 §5 rule 10 (Observable
  operation) and Module 3's test discipline can be satisfied by
  the implementation without a schema slot at v0.1.
- `spec.permissions` / `spec.resources` — memo23 §5 rule 8 and
  Module 6 operational concerns apply when a capsule needs them;
  the greeting needs neither.

In all cases the rule is "optional until a capsule actually needs
it", so Modules 2–4 can be taught against the smallest field set.
:::

## 6. A capsule YAML and a Python module implementing the capability are two different things. Which one belongs in `open-engineering-capsules/source`, and which belongs in `open-engineering-capsule/source`?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="Show answer"}
The **capsule YAML** (the contract) belongs in
`open-engineering-capsules/source` — the definitions org, which
owns the normative schema, the conformance fixtures, and the
`spec.capability` / version-compatibility rules (memo2 §1 D1).

The **implementation** belongs in
`open-engineering-capsule/source` — the implementation org, which
ships the reference validator and any capsule implementation
behind its contract. The Academy consumes whichever conventions
those two repositories publish and does not fork or shadow them
(memo23 §3.2).
:::
